statement: China's CXMT has begun small-batch production of HBM3E, one generation behind SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron, with broader commercial availability targeted for 2027.
why: A fourth HBM source, even a lagging one, starts to relieve the memory bottleneck that currently caps how many accelerators the industry can build.

impact.mechanism: New domestic HBM output, initially tiny and yield-constrained, adds an additional memory source for China-market accelerators and over time nibbles at the three-supplier bottleneck.

evidence.excerpt: CXMT has begun low-volume production of HBM3E chips, currently one generation behind global leaders SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron

confidence.basis: Single secondary outlet relaying a report; low yields and equipment sanctions are stated headwinds, and no company confirmation was fetched.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: statement/trend changed (trend rising -> rising); sources: Investing.com, Investing.com (citing Herald Economy)
